description: Standalone crop dialog -- a separately importable async function that opens a modal crop UI and returns the cropped blob, without requiring image-input

userStories.title: Create cropDialog function with full open/save/cancel flow
userStories.description: As a consumer who owns an image through some means other than image-input, I want to call a single async function that opens a crop dialog and returns the cropped blob, so I do not have to rebuild the dialog shell, save/cancel wiring, and getBlob sequencing from scratch.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/crop-dialog.ts exports an async function (cropDialog or similar) that returns Promise<Blob | null>
Function accepts an image source: File, Blob, or string (object URL or same-origin URL)
Function accepts an optional config object with: heading text, save label, cancel label, and crop constraint (free-form, constrain, ratio literal, or circle)
Calling the function creates a <dialog> containing an <image-crop>, a heading, and Save/Cancel buttons, and opens it as a modal
For File input: passes it to ImageCrop.setFile(). For Blob input: converts to File via toFile() then calls setFile(). For string input: sets the crop element src attribute directly
The crop constraint from the options is forwarded to the <image-crop> element via setAttribute('crop', ...)
Save calls getBlob() on the crop element and resolves the promise with the resulting blob
A second Save click while getBlob() is in flight is ignored (double-submit guard)
Cancel button, Escape key, and clicking the backdrop all close the dialog and resolve the promise with null
The dialog and its contents are removed from the DOM after it closes
Default heading/button text matches the existing crop dialog copy from DEFAULT_TEXT in dialogs.ts (heading: 'Crop image', save: 'Save', cancel: 'Cancel')
The function does not inject any styles -- it expects the consumer to have loaded the crop CSS
The function imports ImageCrop from ./crop.js and toFile from ./file.js but does not import from ./index.js
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Pattern for the save handler exists in client.ts lines 227-256. Pattern for dialog markup exists in dialogs.ts cropDialogMarkup(). The dialog element should use aria-label for accessibility, matching the pattern in dialogs.ts (no id attributes). Buttons sit in <li> wrappers inside a <menu>, matching the existing dialog markup convention.

userStories.title: Add crop-dialog subpath export to package.json
userStories.description: As a consumer, I want to import the cropDialog function from image-input/crop-dialog so I can use it without pulling in the full image-input component.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json exports map includes a ./crop-dialog entry with types, import, and require fields pointing to dist/crop-dialog.d.ts, dist/crop-dialog.js, and dist/crop-dialog.cjs respectively
The new export entry follows the same structure as the existing ./crop export
npm run build (or the project build command) succeeds and produces the dist files
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Model the export entry on the existing ./crop entry in package.json. The build tool should pick up the new entry point automatically if it follows the same pattern.

userStories.title: Add tests for cropDialog function
userStories.description: As a developer, I want tests covering the cropDialog function's key behaviors so regressions are caught automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Test file exists at test/crop-dialog.ts (following the existing test file naming convention)
Test: calling cropDialog with a File opens a modal dialog containing an image-crop element
Test: clicking Save resolves the promise with a Blob
Test: clicking Cancel resolves the promise with null
Test: the dialog element is removed from the DOM after closing
Test: the crop constraint option is forwarded as an attribute on the image-crop element
Test: custom heading and button labels appear in the dialog markup
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow the testing patterns in the existing test/ directory. The tests need a DOM environment since the function creates dialog elements. Check test/fixture.ts and test/crop.ts for how the existing tests set up their environment.
